sections.title: Start here
sections.description: Can code grow restrained, symmetric, slightly mouldy jewellery in the spirit of your own pieces? These 25 are the curator's picks across every approach — growth, simulation, learned lace, threads, sigils, sacred geometry — click one to scrub its process and re-roll it live.

sections.title: AI as editor
sections.description: Before/after pairs: one of the user's selections plus a natural-language edit request, carried out by a Claude agent with the gridlab CLI (+ Jev routing via gl ask).

designs.title: before: half-drawn single_1
designs.notes: single_1 with right-top + bottom-right erased (draw --off fill-rect) and a few asymmetric scribbles (set --on/--off): a simulated half-finished drawing.

designs.title: "complete the symmetry"
designs.notes: gl ask 'complete the symmetry' -> Jev: symmetrize 0.71 -> CANDIDATES (d2 / d4, both auto-trimmed). Picked d2 (gl pick). Jev routed RIGHT (op + d2 candidate); the d4 candidate made no sense for an 11x21 portrait shape. TL scribbles are kept as intended changes, stray right-side scribbles discarded. 5 pieces -> 1.

designs.title: before: multi_1
designs.notes: Sample multi_1 as selected (3 layers).

designs.title: "add a frame on the bottom layer, 1-cell gap"
designs.notes: gl ask -> frame --layer 4 (conf 0.96, auto-applied). Jev routed RIGHT (op and bottom layer) but ignored '1-cell gap': default d=1 touches the lace. undo + gl op frame --layer 4 d=2. Frame is a separate piece on L4 (the gap requires it).

designs.title: before: single_ring
designs.notes: Sample single_ring (1 layer, D4).

designs.title: "a small 4-fold motif in the middle, new top layer"
designs.notes: gl ask -> motif --layer 3 (conf 0.94, auto-applied): op plausible but WRONG layer (wrote into the ring layer, ignored 'new top layer') and kind=cross is not 4-fold. undo; layer add 2; tried motif kind=plus/star/lozenge/orb and kufic (too clip-art / boxy); final: variants of 'motif kind=plus rx=2 ry=2 --region 13,14,19,20 ; grow-coral n=3 reach=2 kind=d4' on L2, picked seed 6: a small mouldy D4 rosette echoing the ring's texture. Note: floats over empty space (support 0) - needs a backplate to be glued.

designs.title: before: single_2
designs.notes: Sample single_2 (1 layer).

designs.title: "make the ends more mouldy, keep it symmetric"
designs.notes: gl ask -> HANDOFF (noise-fill 0.29 / grow-coral / grow-dla): reasonable. trim margin=3 (centre the design); variants of 'grow-dla --region 0,0,18,9 n=6 reach=3 kind=x ; mirror axis=y keep=top' (grow only the top end, mirror to the bottom), picked seed 1. grow-coral variant was tried first but closed the inner loops (too blobby).

designs.title: before: multi_2
designs.notes: Sample multi_2 (3 layers; L5 bottom is a solid plate under the cross).

designs.title: "one blob in the middle - make it lacier, keep the cross"
designs.notes: gl ask -> HANDOFF (height-threshold 0.25, lace-clean, skeleton). Interpreted 'the blob' as the solid L5 plate showing through the middle (L4 is already lace). worley-edges variants stayed blobby; outline d=0 removed little. Final: trim margin=1 (centre), sym-thin --layer 5 -> L5 is a thin double-barred spine; L3 cross untouched.

designs.title: before: single_1
designs.notes: Sample single_1 (1 layer), trimmed.

designs.title: "turn this into a 3-layer piece"
designs.notes: gl ask -> HANDOFF (height-threshold 0.35): fine for an open request. Composition (like the user's own multi_1): bottom = frame around the lace, middle = original lace, top = small plain cross. contrast-layer motif=cross merge=False (lace moved to L4, cross on L3); pad n=1; frame --layer 5 d=1; variants grow-coral n=8 reach=3 kind=d2 on L5, picked seed 3; clear --region on the outside legs (looked like insect legs), trim. merge=True and derive-backplate were tried and rejected (filled the lace / solid plate).

designs.title: before: multi_1
designs.notes: Sample multi_1: L3 is 5 pieces.

designs.title: "connect the loose pieces, one piece per layer"
designs.notes: gl ask -> connect (conf 0.93, applied to all layers): RIGHT op, but broke symmetry (canvas off-centre: symx 0.18) and also edited L4 (per group). undo; trim margin=1; merge-groups --layer 3; connect --layer 3 -> +4 cells, symmetric, 1 piece. (connect without merge-groups worked per group: +22 cells and still 2 pieces.)

designs.title: before: single_ring
designs.notes: Sample single_ring (140 cells).

designs.title: "less busy - thin by a third, keep the rhythm"
designs.notes: gl ask -> HANDOFF (break-2x2 vs sym-thin order disagreement). trim margin=2; spur-prune n=2 (-32: tip tendrils gone, half of the little loops kept); set --off '4,6 6,4' --mirror xy (knob spurs at the diagonals). 140 -> 100 cells (-29%), 4 calm arcs with a knot pair each. Rejected: opening all loops by hand (lost the beading).

sections.title: Algorithm from a sketch
sections.description: A rough structure drawn by hand (frame, spine, a few nodes) turned organic by growth ops — the 'give me an input, make it organic' tool.

designs.title: sketch: oval + cross
designs.notes: Hand sketch: draw ellipse 10,14 8,12 + two lines (Latin cross).

designs.title: oval + cross, grown
designs.notes: dilate n=1 conn=8; noise-fill scale=0.45 threshold=0.5 kind=x; connect max_len=4; skeleton; mirror axis=x keep=left; remove-small (picked seed 3) then grow-coral n=12 reach=2 scale=0.5 kind=x; lace-clean (seed 2). Plain grow-coral/grow-dla on the sketch only added orthogonal stubs.

designs.title: ring + four nodes, grown
designs.notes: grow-coral n=10 reach=3 scale=0.5 kind=d4; lace-clean (picked seed 7 of 8): the nodes become lace knots, the ring stays legible.

designs.title: sketch: spine + ribs
designs.notes: Hand sketch: draw line spine + 4 rib lines on the left, mirror axis=x.

designs.title: spine + ribs, grown
designs.notes: grow-coral n=22 reach=3 scale=0.5 kind=x; lace-clean (picked seed 8 of 8): coral tree-of-life.

sections.title: Mould meets the sacred
sections.description: Exact ancient structures - kamea sigils, the Tree of Life, the Cretan labyrinth, kolam threads, relic windows - handed to living processes: slime mould feeding on the sephirot, lightning aimed at a glyph, coral that eats a labyrinth but never its path. The symbol is the skeleton, the growth its servant; watch the frames.

designs.title: Chiseled paths between sacred points

Top = node rings, middle = tree, base = the plate frozen while it still held 45% extra material (a fossil of the process).

sections.title: Basics
sections.description: The baseline every other section has to beat: mirrored random cells in a capsule. Symmetry alone is not enough - this is what 'too random' looks like.

crystal_sigil.title: Crystal sigil
crystal_sigil.description: Own idea: grow a crystal from a tiny symmetric seed glyph with a 'B1'-family rule (a cell is born next to exactly 1/3/... live cells) while forbidding any birth that would close a 2x2 block. Cells never die, so growth rings are nested: generations double as layers (old core on top, young fringe at the bottom) - an arcane snowflake/sigil.

folded_rule.title: Folded rule frame
folded_rule.description: A mirror-symmetric elementary CA (rule 90/150/18/...) unrolled inward over concentric rings of the silhouette: ring k = generation k. Seeds on the outer ring grow into Sierpinski-like lace that stops after `depth` rings, leaving a calm interior (empty or a motif).

life_lace.title: Life-like CA → lace
life_lace.description: The refined version: the CA's blobs are traced as outlines (or thinned to skeletons), thinned symmetrically to 1-cell strokes, spur-pruned and cleaned by the lace grammar (no 2x2 blocks, no dust). Several sub-runs are scored (one piece, ~30% fill, diagonal wiggle) and the best is kept. Coral/Day&Night/Stains become mould-like tendrils.

life_like.title: Life-like CA (raw)
life_like.description: A Life-like rule (Maze, Mazectric, Coral, Day&Night, Diamoeba, Assimilation, Anneal, ...) run for a few generations from symmetric noise inside a silhouette. Raw output: shows what each rule 'wants' to make before any lace cleanup.

margolus.title: Margolus melt
margolus.description: Block CA on alternating 2x2 partitions (Critters / Tron). A bold symmetric motif (frame + cross) is 'melted' for a few steps: the reversible rule frays its edges into ladders and gliders. Even canvas sizes keep the mirror symmetry exact.

sample_echo.title: Sample echo
sample_echo.description: Loads samples/<name>.json unchanged (the user's reference design).

symmetric_noise.title: Symmetric noise
symmetric_noise.description: Random cells inside a capsule, mirrored D2 (left/right + top/bottom). Optional cleanup removes isolated specks.

coral_seeds.title: Coral seeds
coral_seeds.description: Invasion percolation in a ring band: from a few seeds per 1/8 wedge the coral always creeps into the cheapest neighbouring cell of a smooth noise field, but only where the lace rule allows (no 2x2, at most one orthogonal neighbour). D4 symmetric.

dla_reliquary.title: DLA reliquary
dla_reliquary.description: Diffusion-limited aggregation (or dielectric breakdown / Lichtenberg with exponent eta) grown from a small motif (cross, ring, dot, spine) inside a silhouette; every stick adds a whole mirror orbit and growth stops at a target fill, so it stays restrained.

lichen_rim.title: Lichen rim
lichen_rim.description: A lichen crust creeping inward from the silhouette's rim: lace-rule invasion growth whose resistance rises with depth, so the crust is dense at the edge and frays into tendrils toward a calm centre that holds a small cross.

venation_spine.title: Venation spine
venation_spine.description: Space colonisation (Runions leaf venation) on the grid: veins grow from a central spine toward mirrored attractor points scattered in the outer band. Layers: dilated veins as backplate, the veins, and the spine with dots at vein tips on top.

chiseled_paths.title: Chiseled paths between sacred points
chiseled_paths.description: Start from a solid plate holding the sacred points (Tree of Life or the eight bagua points round a centre) and chisel it away cell by cell in noise order, never cutting the points apart. What remains is a random Steiner root system; a few cells are put back to braid small loops.

circuit_sutra.title: Circuit sutra
circuit_sutra.description: Digital monasticism: the 22 paths of the Tree of Life routed like copper traces - octilinear A* with turn penalties, one cell of clearance, mirrored nets routed once. The sephirot are vias; the base is a ground pour with isolation moats, so every trace is engraved into the plate.

dla_monstrance.title: DLA monstrance
dla_monstrance.description: A reliquary for an absent relic: the oval window in the middle is a reserved void with a moat. Around it a collar, and from the collar a crystalline glory grows outward (DLA-like dielectric breakdown) toward the frame - the monstrance's sunburst, grown rather than drawn.

kolam_eaten.title: Kolam eaten by mould
kolam_eaten.description: The threshold after the rain: a perfect single-thread kolam is washed out where a slime mould's trail runs strongest (never more than a third of it, never at the crossings), then the slime regrows from the cut ends along its own trail. The base keeps the memory of the whole loop.

kolam_excavation.title: The mould remembers the kolam
kolam_excavation.description: A buried single-thread kolam, uncovered by a breathing mould: each pulse the mould creeps outward (lace-rule invasion growth) and everywhere it touched, the kolam's line surfaces; then it retracts to its veins and the tide mark where it stalled. The ancient thread is revealed ring by ring.

lichtenberg_annunciation.title: Lichtenberg annunciation
lichtenberg_annunciation.description: Divine lightning: dielectric breakdown grows down from a halo at the top. The glyph below is held at full potential and the walls are insulating, so the discharge is drawn to it and the growth ends when it strikes.

mandorla_skin.title: Mandorla skin
mandorla_skin.description: The almond of glory as living skin: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion runs only in a band just inside the vesica, so coral grows round a calm icon. The pattern is thresholded at three levels: the full skin below, its thinned veins above, the figure and the hottest spots on top.

overgrown_labyrinth.title: Overgrown labyrinth
overgrown_labyrinth.description: A Cretan labyrinth in a petri dish: its outer wall is eaten (cells removed by noise, never splitting it) and coral mould creeps out of the wound into the dish. The walking path is a reserved void: nothing ever grows in it, so the pilgrimage stays readable.

sigil_mycelium.title: Sigil mycelium
sigil_mycelium.description: A name traced through the Mars kamea as a bilateral seal; mould (lace-rule invasion percolation) is planted at the sigil's vertices and spreads around it, but a 1-cell moat keeps every stroke legible - the mould touches the sigil only where it feeds, at the vertices.

tree_of_life_physarum.title: Tree of Life physarum
tree_of_life_physarum.description: The ten sephirot as food: slime-mould agents (Jones physarum, 4x grid) spawn at the nodes and discover tubes between them. Dangling hair is pruned until every tube runs node to node - the slime's own version of the 22 paths. Da'at stays an empty ring.

tree_writes_name.title: The tree writes the name
tree_writes_name.description: Space colonisation (leaf venation) from a root at the foot of the pendant. Most attractors sit on the strokes of a hidden bindrune made from the name, a few in the margin: the veins grow up and, without knowing it, spell the sigil. The trunk and glyph-tracing main branches stand on top.

layer_composer.title: Layer composer
layer_composer.description: Runs any other recipe to get one lace layer, then derives a 2-4 layer stack with a chosen strategy. With strategy=by_seed each seed shows the SAME lace under a different strategy, so the gallery row is a lesson in composition. Frames show the stack being built.

terraced_relief.title: Terraced relief
terraced_relief.description: A soft relief from one lace: the hull is cut into 3 nested levels by a smooth symmetric field; each level up keeps only the lace inside it with more tendrils pruned, plus the level's own rim. Upper layers sit exactly on lower lace (nested, fully supported) and read as a brighter, calmer core rising out of busier lace.

sample_echo_anneal.title: Sample echo
sample_echo_anneal.description: Lace learned from your samples grown inside a silhouette band; only the quarter is free, the rest is mirrored. method=vote (patch voting, most organic), mrf (refined annealing), mrf-raw (the naive 3x3 annealer: crystallises into ladders). Frames show the texture settling as T drops.

sample_echo_cross.title: Sample echo + cross
sample_echo_cross.description: Learned lace around a crisp central motif (cross/spine/star/eye...) with a one-cell breathing gap and a few bridges, stacked like your multi_1/multi_2: bottom lace, middle lace + motif, top plain motif.

wfc_ring.title: Learned WFC ring
wfc_ring.description: Overlapping-model Wave Function Collapse trained on your lace (3x3 patterns, D4-augmented). Whole symmetry orbits collapse at once so the result is exactly mirrored; crisper than the annealer.

kogin_rosette.title: Kogin rosette
kogin_rosette.description: A 4-fold grammar of concentric diamonds (kogin-zashi / sashiko feel): each ring gets a stitch style (line, stepped, dashed, teeth, little flowers, double), rings are tied by rays along the axes or diagonals, with a small centre glyph. Crisp and calm: a natural top layer or brooch.

name_sigil.title: Hitomezashi name sigil
name_sigil.description: Own idea: hitomezashi (Japanese 'one-stitch' sashiko) as a sigil. The letters of a word are hashed into two bit rows; each bit decides whether a row/column of running stitches starts on or off. Stitches are cells between lattice nodes, so strokes are 1 cell wide and never form 2x2 blocks. Mirrored bit rows make it symmetric; a silhouette crops it into an amulet.

truchet_sparse.title: Sparse Truchet
truchet_sparse.description: Pixel Truchet tiles on a lattice where neighbours share connector cells: fine grain = 3x3 tiles of diagonal arcs, elbows and tiny rings (pure slime-mould bridges); coarse = 5x5 tiles with Smith double-arcs, bridges and beads. Chosen on the fundamental quadrant only, edge-matched so every stroke continues (chains and loops instead of stubs), sparse, inside a silhouette, then mirrored cell-exactly.

bagua_taijitu.title: Bagua ring around the taijitu
bagua_taijitu.description: The eight trigrams in Fu Xi (Earlier Heaven) order - complements facing each other, so the ring is anti-symmetric under a half turn - each on its own plate spoked to a circle around a yin-yang that is literally two layers. Lace only in the outermost band.

magic_walk_rose.title: Magic-walk rose (kamea 1..n²)
magic_walk_rose.description: Every planetary square has an intrinsic route: visit 1, 2, 3 ... n² in order. Associative squares (Saturn, Mars, Venus, Moon) give routes that are already symmetric under a half turn; drawn with octilinear dog-legs and optionally folded by mirrors they become star-roses. Compartment centres are the raised beads, the frame a pixel circle.

monas_stack.title: Monas stack
monas_stack.description: John Dee's hieroglyphic monad and the planetary signs as a grammar: stack 3-4 primitives (horns, circle, circle+dot, cross, double cross, triangles, bar, Aries horns) on one axis - new planets, impossible elements, a lost alphabet - in a mandorla with a thin lace band.

pentecost_corona.title: Pentecost corona
pentecost_corona.description: A demoscene fire effect turned icon nimbus: heat flows outward ring by ring from a source circle (mean of the inner neighbours, minus decay, plus symmetric noise); only the flame edges are kept, so the field becomes lace. D4 halo or a D1 flame crown.

pixel_yantra.title: Pixel yantra
pixel_yantra.description: Bhupura (three nested square lines with T-gates), a circle, an 8- or 16-petal lotus and interlocked triangles around a bindu: a meditation diagram on graph paper. Triangle edges are octilinear (or knight-step), so the Sri-Yantra concurrency problem is exact for free.

cretan_labyrinth.title: Cretan labyrinth
cretan_labyrinth.description: The classical 7-circuit labyrinth from its level sequence 0 3 2 1 4 7 6 5 8, walls one connected piece hanging off the turning spine. show=path raises the walk itself as the thread.

hitomezashi_hexagram.title: Hitomezashi hexagram oracle
hitomezashi_hexagram.description: Cast a hexagram (three coins, seeded); its 6 lines palindromised become the stitch words, so each of the 64 hexagrams owns one loop-sigil. Loop above, hexagram bars below, on a capsule.

hitomezashi_mantra.title: Hitomezashi mantra
hitomezashi_mantra.description: A mantra (or a name) folded into two palindromic bit-words; the stitches decide the sigil. The stitched field inside a disc, with the closed loops at the centre raised as 'the answer'.

hitomezashi_nest.title: Hitomezashi nest (stacked loops)
hitomezashi_nest.description: Own idea: hitomezashi words that make concentric closed loops (Thue-Morse, Fibonacci, pi, text); all closed loops, grouped by distance from the centre, are dealt to the physical layers so the innermost loops stand highest on a bridged bed of all loops.

ice_ray_window.title: Ice-ray shrine window
ice_ray_window.description: Chinese cracked-ice lattice (Stiny's ice-ray grammar, octilinear cuts) in a pointed shrine niche, mirrored; a moon gate (pixel circle) is left whole at the centre as a calm focus.

labyrinth_oracle.title: Labyrinth oracle
labyrinth_oracle.description: Every seed (or text) chooses a different *valid* one-axis labyrinth: level sequences enumerated by DFS with the nested-or-disjoint rule on each side of the axis. Pure architecture.

tocapu_bracelet.title: Tocapu thunder bracelet
tocapu_bracelet.description: A frieze of Andean tocapu units (13x13, quadrant grammar: C4 / D2 / C2 / C2-inverted over step-fret, stair, checker, cross... primitives; no two units alike) separated by step-fret thunder columns. Mirrored about its centre (p2mm feel).

xor_mandala.title: XOR mandala
xor_mandala.description: Munching-squares arithmetic as a mandala: a bitwise formula at x=|dx|, y=|dy| is D4 for free (Sierpinski cross, popcount lattices, xor moire). formula=seeded draws from a curated dozen.

asemic_codex.title: Asemic codex tablet
asemic_codex.description: A fragment of a language that never existed: an alphabet of 16 octilinear glyphs (3x3 node lattice, <= 1 crossing, shared radicals, unique under D4) hung from headlines like Devanagari, three rows in a framed tablet, the centre glyph raised in a cartouche.

bindrune_reliquary.title: Bindrune reliquary
bindrune_reliquary.description: Two or three runes bound on one stave, mirrored into perfect symmetry, set inside a halo with coral (lace-rule invasion growth) outside it.

geomantic_layers.title: Geomantic layer code
geomantic_layers.description: The four rows of one geomantic figure (fire, air, water, earth) switch the four physical layers: odd = one ring, even = a pair of kissing rings, shrinking upward. The stack is the figure.

geomantic_shield.title: Geomantic shield
geomantic_shield.description: A full geomantic chart cast from a question: Mothers -> Daughters (transpose) -> Nieces, Witnesses and the Judge by XOR. Nieces, Witnesses and Judge stand as figures on plates in an inverted pyramid (the heraldic shield) hung in an open shield frame; Mothers and Daughters form a frieze of small figures above. The Judge rises on a fourth layer.

kamea_seal.title: Kamea seal
kamea_seal.description: A name traced through a planetary magic square (Agrippa): Latin gematria, zeros dropped until the number fits, a ring where the route starts and a bar where it ends. BASE is the square as a grille (frame + compartment lattice + the route's shadow) - the map; MID the route; TOP the marks.

kufic_pinwheel.title: Kufic pinwheel seal
kufic_pinwheel.description: Square-Kufic grammar as a hard rule - no 2x2 window all ink or all void - annealed under quarter-turn symmetry from concentric squares into a pinwheel of meanders: a word you can't quite read. Toothed frame, raised ascenders.

ogham_spine.title: Ogham spine
ogham_spine.description: The wearer's name in Ogham on the pendant's spine (read bottom to top): B-aicme short bars, H-aicme long bars, M-aicme rising chevrons, vowels as dot pairs - the same 'spine with bars' the user draws, but personal. Learned lace on both sides.

spare_reliquary.title: Spare monogram reliquary
spare_reliquary.description: Austin Osman Spare's method: strip a desire to its unique consonants, overlay them in an octilinear stroke font (seeded flips), optionally mirror into a mute glyph - then house it like a relic: a plate inside an elliptic halo, coral lace grown off the halo inside a vesica.

veve_scaffold.title: Vèvè scaffold with the one mark
veve_scaffold.description: A pole-centred ground-drawing grammar (inspired by the structure of vèvè, not copying any lwa's sign): a central pole, decreasing crossbars, square-spiral scrolls at the bar ends, diagonal flourishes, finishing points scattered along the outer contour - and one deliberate asymmetric mark.

cave_skeleton.title: Cave skeleton
cave_skeleton.description: Symmetric noise at 2x resolution smoothed by a majority-rule CA into rounded caves, then Zhang-Suen thinned: the medial lines form closed mould cells. The pre-thinning blobs are the backplate.

gray_scott_band.title: Gray-Scott band
gray_scott_band.description: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion on a 4x grid with no-flux edges; the kill rate rises past an outer band so the pattern dies out and the interior stays calm. One field, thresholded at 2-3 levels, gives nested layers: the wide coral at the bottom, its cores above.

physarum_feeding.title: Physarum feeding
physarum_feeding.description: Jeff Jones' slime-mould model: agents sense, turn toward and deposit trail on a 4x finer grid; food sits at the cross ends and at points on the frame, so the mould grows tubes that link motif to frame. Trail mirror-averaged each step, then pooled, thresholded and thinned.

pulse_mould.title: Pulsing mould
pulse_mould.description: A mould that breathes: each pulse it creeps outward (lace-rule invasion growth) to a new radius, then retracts, keeping only its main veins and the tide mark where the front stalled. Repeated pulses leave concentric broken rings tied together by veins, like a sigil.

celtic_panel.title: Celtic knot panel
celtic_panel.description: Interlace panel: rotated mirror-curve lattice (orthogonal woven bands, '+' crossings, chamfered walls) fitted to a rounded panel, held in a frame by 4 axis tabs; true over/under as a raised layer.

kolam_interlace.title: Kolam interlace: over and under
kolam_interlace.description: The single thread woven over and under itself in physical layers: strict alternation (every strand goes over, under, over...). Lunda-plate base, curve, raised over-bridges.

lusona_lunda.title: Lusona thread and its Lunda design
lusona_lunda.description: Chokwe sand-drawing logic: a plaited mat of dots made into one thread; walking the thread and colouring its quarter-arcs by parity gives a Lunda design (Gerdes), drawn as a two-tone piece: blocks plate below, the design's 1-cell skeleton raised on top.

name_kolam.title: Name kolam (a threshold for a name)
name_kolam.description: Own idea: the dot rows are spelled by the text (palindromised bits -> row widths) and the seed comes from the text, so every name has exactly one single-thread kolam.

sikku_kolam.title: Sikku kolam: the single thread
sikku_kolam.description: Pulli kolam: one unbroken line circling every dot (diamond 1-3-5-7-5-3-1 by default). Pitch-6 diagonal raster with real pulli dots; base plate = the loop's own silhouette.

thread_reliquary.title: Thread reliquary (kolam around a void cross)
thread_reliquary.description: Own idea: the dot set is a capsule with a cross of missing dots, so the single thread must circle an empty cross (a meaningful void). A spine-and-bar runs under the thread and shows through the void, carrying a raised cross.

diagonal_maze.title: Braided diagonal maze
diagonal_maze.description: A uniform spanning tree (Wilson) grown on the diagonal node lattice of a silhouette band, so every link renders as a thin diagonal bridge: pure slime-mould lace. Leaves pruned, a few loops braided in, then mirrored; optional dashed frame and central motif.

void_lace.title: Void lace (reliquary)
void_lace.description: Out of the box: lace (learned or worms) grows everywhere EXCEPT a reserved channel around a hidden motif, so the cross/eye/star is drawn by absence. With 2 layers a back plate shaped like the void shows through it in a darker tone, like a relic behind lace.

worm_lace.title: Worm lace
worm_lace.description: Curling random walkers (continuous heading + angular velocity, rasterised) crawl on mirrored orbits; a step is refused if it would make a 2x2 block or touch another strand (except rare diagonal joins). Frames show them crawl.
